headline_marked: [[Connected Cars]] Share Vast Amounts of Personal Data, Study Finds
headline: Connected Cars Share Vast Amounts of Personal Data, Study Finds
summary: A new study analyzed 21 vehicles and 30 companion apps, revealing extensive data sharing with manufacturers and undisclosed third parties.
details: Over 75% of vehicles sold globally now come with built-in internet access, enabling constant communication with manufacturers and external companies. This connectivity, while offering convenience, raises significant privacy concerns.

Researchers from Northeastern University partnered with Consumer Reports to test 21 late-model vehicles and their companion mobile apps. The study aimed to understand the privacy implications of this connected vehicle ecosystem.

The findings indicate that both vehicles and their associated apps transmit substantial amounts of private consumer data to various first and third-party servers. This data sharing occurs over Wi-Fi and cellular connections.

A key concern highlighted is that once data reaches these servers, companies may share or sell it to other undisclosed third parties. Consumers reportedly have little to no control over their data once it leaves their devices.

The study employed detailed experimental methods, including setting up custom access points to log vehicle traffic and using Faraday tents to test how blocking cellular signals affects data transmission over Wi-Fi.

While the study covered a wide range of vehicles, it did not include every manufacturer in the U.S. market. The results represent a snapshot in time and may not be generalizable to all connected vehicles.

headline_marked: SvelteKit 3 [[officially launches]] with new remote functions and improved type safety
headline: SvelteKit 3 officially launches with new remote functions and improved type safety
summary: The latest version of the Svelte application framework is here, promising a more polished and type-safe development experience with seamless migration tools.
details: SvelteKit 3.0 has officially been released, offering developers a more refined and type-safe application framework for Svelte projects. The update focuses on reducing unnecessary elements and enhancing the overall development experience.

Migration from earlier versions is designed to be as smooth as possible, with the 'sv migrate' command automatically handling much of the codebase. A TODO list will be generated for any remaining manual adjustments.

Key new features include 'remote functions', a utility set for secure, efficient, and type-safe client-server communication. This functionality requires Async Svelte, which currently needs an experimental flag to be enabled.

While SvelteKit 3 introduces some breaking changes, these are detailed in the official migration guide. The release aims to provide a more robust and streamlined development workflow for Svelte developers.
The Svelte ecosystem continues to grow, with the next Svelte Summit scheduled for November 19-20 in Ljubljana, Slovenia, also marking Svelte's 10th anniversary.
